| Recent EUR/GBP low | 0.8447 (16- to 17-month low) | 
| 2-week EUR/GBP move | Approximately -1.7% | 
| 10-year France-Germany spread | 137 basis points | 
Light Trading Conditions and Central Bank Speakers
On Monday, market attention is centered on appearances by policymakers from both the European Central Bank (ECB) and the Bank of England (BoE). However, overall liquidity is expected to be thin, with trading volumes likely held down by a long weekend in Japan and a partial holiday in the United States.
Within the Eurozone, a key focal point this week is the scheduled appearance of ECB President Christine Lagarde on Wednesday at a central banking event in Bangkok, Thailand. Market observers will monitor her remarks for any signals regarding the timing of the ECB’s next interest rate adjustment.
UK Data in Focus: Growth and Production
In the United Kingdom, the main event on the economic calendar this week is the release of August Gross Domestic Product (GDP) figures alongside Industrial and Manufacturing Production data on Thursday. These releases are expected to draw heightened scrutiny, as investors look for data that could validate recent hawkish commentary from BoE officials, including Governor Andrew Bailey.
Commentary from analysts at Commerzbank highlights this dynamic. They note that the UK’s “improved growth outlook should make it easier for the Bank of England to raise rates further in order to lean against inflation.” As for the EUR/GBP pair, Commerzbank’s assessment is that they expect “EUR/GBP to trade broadly sideways over the coming months.”
Central Banks: Roles and Policy Framework
Central banks play a central role in maintaining price stability within their respective economies. They monitor inflation and deflation – defined as persistent increases or decreases in the prices of goods and services – and adjust policy to keep aggregate demand aligned with their objectives. Major institutions such as the US Federal Reserve (Fed), the ECB, and the BoE aim to maintain inflation close to 2%.
When inflation deviates from this target, central banks rely primarily on changes to their benchmark policy rate, commonly referred to as the interest rate. At scheduled meetings, they announce any decisions to keep, raise, or lower this rate and provide justification for their stance. Commercial banks respond by adjusting savings and lending rates, which then influences borrowing, investment, and consumption. A pronounced increase in rates is often described as monetary tightening, whereas a reduction in the policy rate is labeled monetary easing.
Decisions on monetary policy are taken by a governing body or policy board that is typically structured to operate independently from day-to-day politics. Candidates for these boards usually pass through multiple screening processes before appointment. Within these bodies, members can differ in their policy preferences. Those favoring low rates and easier financial conditions to support growth, even if inflation runs somewhat above 2%, are commonly referred to as “doves.” Those preferring higher rates to protect savings and keep inflation firmly at or just below 2% are labeled “hawks.”
Most central banks are headed by a chair or president who presides over meetings, works to forge agreement between hawkish and dovish members, and may cast the deciding vote if the committee is split. This figure delivers regular speeches to outline the current policy stance and future outlook. To minimize abrupt market reactions, central banks often communicate their thinking ahead of formal decision days, while observing a “blackout period” just before meetings during which policymakers are not allowed to speak publicly until the new policy decision has been announced.

articles.title: Think Strategically: Year Five of the Bull Market: The Rally That Kept Climbing the Wall of Worry - WJournalpr
articles.summary: Think Strategically: Year Five of the Bull Market: The Rally That Kept Climbing the Wall of Worry  WJournalpr
articles.full_text:
The Weekly Wall Street Recap
U.S. stocks finished higher across the board last week. The S&P 500 gained 1.15% to 7,811.54, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.93% to 51,654.55, and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.64% to 27,366.17, leaving the Nasdaq the strongest of the three so far this year at +17.74%.
Puerto Rico did better still. The Birling Capital PR Stock Index rose 1.41% to 4,832.92 and is now up 22.02% for the year, roughly 7.9 points ahead of the S&P 500. The Birling Capital U.S. Bank Index lagged, adding just 0.16% to 9,411.26 and trailing the broad market at +4.14%. Treasury yields eased slightly, with the 10-year note down 4 basis points to 5.24% and the 2-year down 3 basis points to 4.80%, though both remain well above where they began the year.
That puts the S&P 500 just below the 7,818.93 it reached last Tuesday, when it closed above 7,800 for the first time, and it arrives at a milestone. On October 12, 2022, the index sat roughly 25% below its peak, inflation was above 8%, and the Federal Reserve was hiking at the fastest pace in a generation. Almost nobody was calling a bottom. Four years later, the index has more than doubled and has recorded its 124th all-time high.
The anniversary invites a victory lap. It deserves a closer look, though, because the bull market entering its fifth year looks very different from the one that began it. The Fed is now raising rates, not cutting them. The 10-year Treasury yield has touched about 5.3%, its highest level since 2002. Brent crude is hovering near $100. Yet earnings are growing faster than at any point in decades outside post-recession rebounds.
A solid run, not a record-setter
Measured from the October 2022 low, the S&P 500 has gained about 117% in price, or roughly 130% with dividends. That is impressive but ordinary by historical standards. The eleven bull markets since the late 1950s averaged price gains near 150% and lasted about five years, and six of the eleven ran past the four-year mark. The longest, from 2009 to 2020, lasted almost eleven years.
So age alone is not a warning sign. What sets this cycle apart is the terrain it has crossed: the 2023 regional bank failures, the 2024 yen carry trade unwind, the 2025 tariff correction, and in 2026 a war involving Iran, an oil price shock, and the S&P 500's slide to a closing low of 6,344 on March 30. From that low, the index has rallied about 23%.
Four forces that define this cycle
1. Skepticism never left. Bull markets usually end in euphoria. Recession calls have shadowed this one since its first week. The inverted yield curve, normally a reliable alarm, stayed negative through most of 2022 to 2024, and the recession never came. Growth ran above trend, consumers kept spending, and AI-related investment grew large enough to rival the entire housing sector's fixed investment. The wall of worry is still standing, which is historically more comforting than a market with no doubters.
2. Higher rates are the price of strong growth, and now the main risk. Many investors spent four years waiting for rates to return to 2010s levels. The better question is whether that decade was the anomaly. Government borrowing is heavy, capital spending needs are large, and the Fed's own estimate of the long-run neutral rate has climbed to 3.25%, the highest since 2016.
This is where the story has moved furthest from the original script. In September the Fed raised its target range by a quarter point to 3.75%–4.00%, its first hike since 2023. The updated projections showed 16 of 18 officials expecting at least one more increase this year, with the median year-end rate at about 4.1%. Median 2026 inflation (PCE) is projected at 3.7%, with unemployment at 4.1%. A Fed expected to “tap the brakes” is, by its own projections, still pressing on.
3. AI built the earnings, and the leadership is narrow. Roughly 40 cents of every dollar in the S&P 500 sits in its ten largest companies, and NVIDIA alone accounts for about 8 cents. This concentration has been earned: the biggest names are producing the biggest profit gains. But concentration cuts both ways. It means the index's fate depends heavily on a handful of capital-spending decisions and earnings reports.
4. Earnings have taken over from valuation. About 70% of the gain since 2022 came from higher earnings and 30% from a higher multiple. This year the balance tipped further as multiples eased while profits surged. Analysts expect third-quarter S&P 500 earnings to grow about 29.5% from a year ago, the third straight quarter above 25%. Revenue growth near 12% suggests this is not merely cost cutting. Estimates rose during the quarter, which is unusual, since analysts normally trim them. Fourth-quarter growth is projected near 28%, and full-year 2026 growth is close to 32%
The headwinds worth taking seriously: Three pressures are converging at once.
• The bond market is competing for capital. A 10-year yield above 5% gives investors a credible alternative to equities for the first time in a generation. Stocks have absorbed it so far because earnings are rising, but each new yield high narrows the margin for error.
• The earnings comparison gets harder. Consensus calls for growth to slow to roughly 15% in 2027, with a nearly flat quarter along the way. Markets can handle deceleration, but not disappointment relative to a very high bar.
• The market is overdue for a pause. The S&P 500 has gone close to a year without a 10% pullback. Corrections are routine, and the longer the gap, the less shocking they are.
What the latest U.S. data say: growth cooling, jobs holding
GDPNow shows that the Atlanta Fed's estimate of third-quarter growth fell to an annualized rate of 3.60% in its October 8 update, down from 3.70% on October 6. This is the lowest figure for the quarter, being 2.6 points below the initial estimate of 6.20% given on August 3. The trajectory has been irregular: it fell to 4.00% by August 18, rose to 5.10% on September 17, and then dropped 1.3 points to 3.70% on September 30. It stayed there until October 6, then fell again. Nevertheless, 3.60% is still well above the 2% long-term trend. The economy is still growing strongly, but the model's inputs have been softer than they appeared in early August. GDPNow is a model estimate, not an official forecast, and the estimate will continue to change as new data arrives.
Initial jobless claims. Initial jobless claims fell to 197,000 during the week ending October 3, down 2,000 (1.01%) from 199,000 the previous week. The four-week moving average also fell to 198,000 from 200,500, down 2,500 (1.25%). Claims are now near the year's low. They peaked at 230,000 in early February and again in early June, and hit a low of 189,000 in July. The most recent figure is therefore 33,000 below the peak levels. Employers are still retaining workers, with little evidence of the layoffs that usually occur as the economy slows.
What it means. This means growth is slowing to 3.60%, but the labor market isn't slowing, as shown by the 197,000 figure for initial claims. This is one reason the Federal Reserve has been able to continue tightening. Strong labor market data supports further interest rate hikes rather than fewer; continue tightening.
What to watch between now and year-end
Where this could go: three illustrative scenarios
Year-end targets on Wall Street generally fall between 7,950 and 8,000, representing only about a 2% increase from current levels. Rather than relying on any single forecast, it's worth looking at the underlying figures. Price is roughly equal to earnings multiplied by the multiple investors are willing to pay, and the S&P 500 is currently trading at about 19 times expected earnings. The scenarios below are my own simplified examples covering twelve months, starting with the index near 7,800.
The second case is the most instructive. Even with strong profit growth, a modest loss of one multiple point leaves returns well below the double digits of the past four years. In this phase of the cycle, the multiple matters as much as earnings, and the 10-year Treasury yield largely sets the multiple.
The takeaway
Bull markets rarely die of old age. They end when the Fed tightens too hard, when the economy rolls over, or when earnings fall short of a price that has already assumed perfection. Today, the Fed is tightening, though not yet at a level that is restrictive by historical standards, and earnings still beat expectations. That is a tension, not a verdict.
We believe the onus of proof is changing. During the first three years, investors had to be convinced that the rally was genuine. By the fifth year, the rally itself will have to show it can endure yields above 5% and a Federal Reserve that hasn't finished its work yet. The most likely scenario is a market that keeps rising, but more slowly and with greater turbulence, with returns closer to earnings growth minus some multiple compression rather than the double-digit rates seen in recent years.
The practical implications are that you should anticipate a pullback rather than be surprised by it, regard the concentration among a small number of AI leaders as a risk to be assessed rather than as a trend to be pursued, and keep a close eye on the 10-year yield just as you do on any earnings report.
Puerto Rico Economic Update
Puerto Rico's economy is flat, and the latest figures indicate problems beneath the surface. Growth predictions are near zero, unemployment is at its highest level in the period we have data for, and consumer spending remains weak in motor vehicles, retail, and construction. The only exception is publicly traded companies: the Birling Capital Puerto Rico Stock Index has increased 22.02% this year.

Accessibility tools
Rising oil prices to blame for a surge in global bond yields
12 Oct 2026
Brent Crude Oil breached the $100 a barrel threshold again at the end of Q3, having begun the quarter at $72. The US conflict with Iran seems no closer to a resolution and as a result, global inflation continues to be pushed higher.
Simeon Willis and Emma Coleman explore the key developments shaping markets in our latest Investment Quarterly update.
Quarter in brief
- Oil prices top $100 a barrel by quarter end as war in Iran continues
- Rising yields become a challenge for the UK’s October Budget
- The ECB, BOJ and Fed raise interest rates but BOE holds firm for now
- Equity returns remain positive as AI optimism returns
- Aggregate UK DB pension scheme funding levels rose
Inflation – and thus the growing expectation of further central bank rate rises in the near future – have driven a global bond sell off over the third quarter. The US Treasury took rare measures to intervene in the US Treasuries market over August by announcing it would double its buy backs of long-term government bonds in a bid to contain the rising costs of financing its own debt.
The UK has also felt the pinch of rising borrowing costs ahead of UK Chancellor John Healy’s first Autumn Budget. Fiscal headroom rules have constrained the government’s ability to fund public spending through additional debt and whilst the government has sought to ease some of the spending pressure on households through the removal of VAT on energy bills, tax increases seem likely. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has also committed to ending the state pension triple-lock at the end of the current parliament to help fund a proposed National Care Service as the UK government looks to rebalance its use of public money.
Despite UK Consumer Prices Inflation rising to 3.1% in the 12-months to August, the Bank of England narrowly voted not to increase the bank rate from 3.75% in September. On the other hand, the Federal Reserve (Fed) unanimously voted to increase their interest rate by a quarter percentage point for the first time since 2023. The Fed rate now sits at a range of 3.75% - 4.00% and four more rate rises have been priced into futures markets over the next 12 months.
The European Central Bank (ECB) and Bank of Japan (BOJ) joined the Fed with 0.25% rate increases during the quarter. This was the second rate hike of the year by the ECB, up to 2.5%. The BOJ’s interest rate of 1.25% is the highest it has been for over three decades.
Global equity market performance was positive over the third quarter as AI confidence returned, providing a boost to both developed markets (largely driven by the performance of the US) and emerging markets. UK equities performed particularly well in Q3 thanks to its exposure to financials benefitting from the expectations of higher-for-longer interest rates and the energy sector benefitting from rising global energy supply costs.
UK fixed interest gilt yields rose to their highest levels since 2007 just before the quarter end and so it is no surprise that the asset class performed poorly over the third quarter. Index linked gilts also posted negative returns but were offset by rising long-term inflation expectations. Despite the sell-off in UK gilts, Liability Driven Investment (LDI) recapitalisation activity for UK defined benefit pension schemes has been relatively muted thus far, testament to the improved resilience of the leveraged LDI market since the 2022 mini-budget gilts crisis. UK corporate bonds and global high yield bonds both suffered negative performance as global sovereign bond yields around the globe rose.
Aggregate UK DB pension scheme funding levels on a low risk basis rose thanks to rising yields reducing the present value of their liabilities. This will have been matched to some extent by a fall in liability hedging assets but positive growth asset performance has
helped assets to outpace liabilities overall.
Despite the sell-off in UK gilts, LDI recapitalisation activity for UK defined benefit pension schemes has been relatively muted thus far, testament to the improved resilience of the leveraged LDI market since the 2022 mini-budget gilts crisis.
Simeon Willis, Chief Investment Officer

articles.full_text:
Dollar Index: Inflation Test Keeps Fed Policy in Focus
The dollar remains supported by elevated U.S. borrowing costs and geopolitical tensions, while the focus is on the U.S. inflation report for next direction. Traders currently give a 81% probability of the Fed not changing policy rates at their October meeting, after weaker jobs data lessened the case for an immediate policy hike. Further increases in December or early 2027 remain a possibility if inflation doesn't decline.
Inflation forecasts are for U.S. headline inflation to hit 3.7% and core to be around 2.5% this month. Inflation data this week will be key for the dollar's outlook.
EUR: French Debt Risk Counters ECB Tightening Expectations
These forecasts were made by market participants or market analysts and reported by the source. Forecasts are not guaranteed to actually occur. Forecasts are not a reliable indicator of future performance.
France's fiscal situation still casts a shadow on the euro. The spread on 10-year bonds between France and Germany has risen to about 137 basis points and is approaching the levels last seen in 2012. This highlights the uncertainty in the market regarding France's ability to bring more budgetary discipline in the run up to the 2027 presidential elections.
Some help on monetary policy is expected. A Reuters poll showed that nearly 90% of economists expect the ECB to raise its 2.50% deposit rate by 25 basis points in December following a surge in euro-area inflation.
GBP: Rate-Hike Expectations Meet a Difficult Budget Test
Monetary policy is expected to be tightened in the UK as well with an above 80% chance of a Bank of England rate hike in November.
Fiscal policy is expected to be implemented to help ease the UK's cost-of-living concerns. The IFS estimates the government will need to find about £36 billion through tax rises or welfare cuts in the upcoming Budget on the 28th of October due to higher inflation, pressure on public services and increased defence spending.
U.S. Dollar Index Technical Analysis: DXY Holds Above 102.10 as 102.49 Remains the Key Breakout Level
Currently, the U.S. Dollar Index is trading around 102.24 on the 2-hour chart, and what catches my eye is how price is holding above the rising trendline and both moving averages. The large picture trend remains up, although price repeatedly failing around 102.49 shows that price still needs a clear breakout to push to higher levels.
102.49 is the first major level of resistance, and a break above that would likely bring 102.70, and 102.95 into the picture. Again, 102.10 is a key support, and if price continues to drop, 101.75 and 101.43 would come into play.

articles.title: [不同来源] US dollar strength masks growing disconnect with Treasury yields - FOREX.com
articles.summary: US dollar strength masks growing disconnect with Treasury yields  FOREX.com
articles.full_text:
- DXY's relationship with front-end yields abruptly turns negative
- Euro weakness offsets retreat in Fed tightening expectations
- US CPI backtesting reveals no consistent directional trading advantage
- DXY, EUR/USD and USD/JPY test important technical levels
US dollar resilience faces a busy week
The US dollar enters a busy week for economic data, headlined by CPI, PPI and retail sales on Wednesday and Thursday. However, while those releases will be the headline acts, what may be of greater interest is the abrupt breakdown in the dollar's relationship with front-end US Treasury yields.
Having maintained a generally positive relationship through much of this year, correlations have deteriorated sharply in October, with the dollar continuing to strengthen despite a partial reversal of September's surge in US yields and reduced expectations for further Fed tightening. Without renewed concerns over France's public finances weighing heavily on the euro, it's possible the dollar would already be trading considerably lower.
DXY's relationship with US Treasury yields breaks down
You can see the deterioration in the dollar's relationship with front-end US Treasury yields in the graphic below. As recently as the end of September, the 10-session rolling correlation between DXY and US two-year yields stood at +0.66, with the 20-session measure at +0.55. By the end of last week, those readings had fallen to −0.39 and +0.19, respectively.
Source: LSEG
Similar movements have been seen against five-year yields in the belly of the curve, suggesting the change isn't confined to just the front end. Since the end of September, DXY has risen around 0.75%, despite US two-year yields falling 9.6 basis points and five-year yields declining 6.8 basis points over the same period.
Fed pricing retreats, but the dollar holds firm
Following the softer US payrolls report earlier this month, along with what appears to have been a concerted effort by Fed officials to push back against expectations for another rate hike in October, markets have reduced their expectations for further tightening. As shown in the graphic below, cumulative tightening priced through the end of next year has fallen from just over 100 basis points in mid-September to around 80 basis points.
Source: TradingView
Had the dollar maintained the positive relationship with front-end Treasury yields seen earlier this year, it suggests that, all else being equal, the greenback would be weaker than where it is today.
However, currencies don't trade on US developments alone. Renewed concerns over France's public finances, fears of spillovers into other European debt markets and higher energy prices have weighed heavily on the euro. Given its 57.6% weighting in DXY, that weakness may explain why the dollar has remained so resilient despite the retreat in US rate expectations.
CPI brings volatility, but little directional certainty
While there's plenty of important US economic data coming our way this week, historical patterns offer little guidance on directional risks for the dollar. Backtesting of 188 CPI releases since 2011 shows that although the dollar tends to experience larger moves on inflation reporting days, there's little evidence of a consistent tendency to either extend or reverse its prevailing trend.
That suggests traders should keep a close eye not only on the incoming US data, but also on developments in European debt markets, which may prove just as influential in determining where the dollar heads next.
DXY: Bullish continuation pattern takes shape
Source: TradingView
DXY is consolidating the strong bullish move that began in early September, coinciding with a sharp increase in market expectations for further Fed tightening.
Whether you call it a symmetrical triangle or a bull pennant, the price has now tested both sides of the structure on several occasions, with the trading range continuing to narrow as bullish momentum cools. RSI (14) has been setting lower highs and has returned towards the neutral 50 level, while MACD remains below its signal line, albeit still in positive territory.
Given the preceding rally, the formation suggests we may see an eventual bullish breakout take place, although confirmation is required via a break above the upper boundary of the structure.
The upper boundary of the structure currently sits just below 102.50, with rising trend support located just beneath 102.00. Beyond those levels, 102.535, the high set earlier this month, is the immediate upside level to watch.
A sustained break above 102.535 would strengthen the bullish continuation argument, potentially opening the door to 103.35, which acted as both support and resistance in late 2024 and early 2025. Beyond that, 104.68, the March 2025 swing high, is the next topside level of note.
On the downside, 101.80, the June 24 swing high, has attracted buying on the last two tests from below. Beneath that, 101.60 is another important level, having acted as resistance earlier this year. A break below the latter would put 101.026, the swing low set in late September, in play.
EUR/USD: Downside risks persist despite fading momentum
Source: TradingView
Unsurprisingly, a similar pattern is developing in EUR/USD on the four-hourly timeframe, albeit in the opposite direction. Following the sharp decline since September, the price has been consolidating within a contracting range that resembles either a bear pennant or a symmetrical triangle.
Since bottoming at 1.1162 earlier this month, the price has continued to contract, even as momentum indicators show signs of improvement despite unresolved concerns in French debt markets. RSI (14) has been setting higher lows and has returned to the neutral 50 level, while MACD has crossed above its signal line and is trending higher, albeit remaining marginally in negative territory.
It's a bearish continuation pattern, pointing to the risk of an eventual breakdown, although confirmation is still required.
On the downside, the lower boundary of the structure currently sits around 1.1165, just above the October swing low at 1.1162, making this an important support zone to watch. A breakdown would put 1.1065 in play, the swing low set in May 2025, with little other obvious technical support in between.
Overhead, 1.12429, the high set on Friday, is the immediate level to watch, followed by the upper boundary of the structure around 1.1260. Above that, 1.12855, where the formation began, is the next upside level of note. A break higher would put 1.1312 in play, the late-September low that subsequently gave way during the decline into October.
USD/JPY: Higher lows put resistance under pressure
Source: TradingView
USD/JPY has repeatedly struggled to overcome resistance at 158.45 since early October, including another failed attempt earlier today. However, since bottoming at 156.40 in late September, we've seen a series of higher lows, with buyers stepping in at progressively shallower levels.
It's not quite an ascending triangle, but it has that feel to it, with the price gradually squeezing higher towards horizontal resistance at 158.45. That makes 158.45 the immediate level to watch, with a break above potentially opening the door to 159.00 and 159.50.
On the downside, dips towards 157.50 and below have been bought over the past week, making that the first level to watch, followed by 157.00 and 156.40.

articles.title: Zetwerk sets IPO price band at Rs 143-151; eyes Rs 5,012 Cr from issue - Entrackr
articles.summary: Zetwerk sets IPO price band at Rs 143-151; eyes Rs 5,012 Cr from issue  EntrackrPeak XV, Accel-backed Zetwerk seeks $2.64 billion valuation in India IPO  ReutersZetwerk eyes Rs 2,830 crore fresh issue, boasts Rs 12,500 crore order book  The Times of IndiaZetwerk IPO: Early investors set for up to 38X returns through OFS  EntrackrAbu Dhabi’s ADIA weighs anchor investment in India’s Zetwerk IPO - Report  Zawya
articles.full_text:
Manufacturing platform Zetwerk has fixed the price band for its initial public offering (IPO) at Rs 143-151 per share. The Bengaluru-based company aims to raise around Rs 5,012 crore through the public issue, valuing it at around Rs 25,583 crore at the upper end of the price band.
The IPO will open for subscription on October 15 and close on October 19. The company will open its anchor investor book on October 14, while its shares are expected to list on the stock exchanges on October 23.
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,830 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 14.45 crore shares by promoters and existing investors, according to its red herring prospectus (RHP).
Zetwerk has increased the fresh issue size from Rs 2,600 crore proposed in its updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP) filed in August. The OFS component has also increased by 49% from 9.68 crore shares proposed earlier.
Promoters Amrit Pratik Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan will each sell 1.42 crore shares, while promoter group entity Creovate Innovation will offload up to 2.30 crore shares. Among existing investors, Lightspeed Venture Partners will sell 2.51 crore shares, followed by Peak XV Partners with 2.34 crore shares. Accel India V will also sell up to 1.2 crore shares.
Zetwerk plans to use Rs 1,300 crore from the fresh issue to repay or prepay borrowings at the company level. Another Rs 860 crore will go towards debt repayment at nine subsidiaries. The remaining proceeds will be used for acquisitions, strategic investments and general corporate purposes.
Founded in 2017, Zetwerk operates a technology-led manufacturing platform that connects businesses with manufacturers and suppliers across sectors such as electronics, energy, aerospace, defence and industrial automation.
On the financial front, Zetwerk’s revenue from continuing operations rose to Rs 15,913 crore in FY26 from Rs 11,332 crore in FY25. In Q1 FY27, revenue from operations grew 55% year-on-year to Rs 4,118 crore, while losses from continuing operations narrowed to Rs 64 crore from Rs 881 crore in the year-ago quarter.

articles.title: Chip selloff extends as South Korean stock market sinks 6% - Yahoo Finance
articles.summary: Chip selloff extends as South Korean stock market sinks 6%  Yahoo FinanceSouth Korea's chip-heavy stock market is plunging again as AI investors find more reasons to worry  Business InsiderKorean Chip Stocks Sink on Chinese Rival Worry, Broadcom Remarks  Bloomberg.comSouth Korea’s Kospi index sinks more than 7% on semiconductor share sell-off over AI boom worries  NBC NewsNews by CNBC TV18 on TradingView, 2026-10-13 — cnbctv:570cb7159094b:0  Trad...
articles.full_text:
Shares of Micron (MU) and SK Hynix (SKHY) are poised to open lower on Tuesday, extending a global sell-off in memory-chip stocks as South Korea's benchmark KOSPI (^KS11I) tanked 6%.
In South Korea, SK Hynix (000660.KS) and Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) each fell roughly 8%, extending their losing streaks to five sessions. The two chipmakers account for more than half of the South Korean stock market's total capitalization.
The sell-off was a continuation of market reaction after Chinese memory maker CXMT (688825.SS) announced progress on a new memory-cell design engineered to pack more storage into less physical space.
CXMT aims to introduce a new server memory product built on this architecture by the end of 2026.
The advance threatens to intensify competition for Samsung, SK Hynix, and US-based Micron, which together account for roughly 90% of the global DRAM market.
Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung have been major beneficiaries of the AI trade over the past year amid surging demand for memory and storage chips driven by the global AI data center build-out. All three memory makers reached $1 trillion valuation over the summer.
Last week, Samsung reported a preliminary record third quarter profit of $80 billion, but the forecast did little to lift the rest of the chip sector,
Micron posted strong quarterly results in September. The stock is up roughly 240% year-to-date.

articles.title: Equity mutual fund inflows rise 31% in September; small-cap schemes hit all-time high - CNBC TV18
articles.summary: Equity mutual fund inflows rise 31% in September; small-cap schemes hit all-time high  CNBC TV18India's monthly fund investments hit record highs despite market slide  ReutersSIPs register recorded ₹32,490 crore of inflows in September 2026  The HinduInvestors shrug off bear party, put big money into equity mutual funds  The Economic TimesDespite volatility in September, SIP flows hit new high of 32.5k crore  The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Equity mutual fund inflows rose 30.6% to ₹38,293.5 crore in September, driven by an all-time high in small-cap schemes. Total industry AUM stood at ₹82.64 lakh crore, while gold ETFs saw a 71.4% surge in inflows.
Equity mutual fund schemes attracted net inflows of ₹38,293.5 crore in September, up 30.6% from ₹29,315 crore in August, according to data from the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI).
Small-cap funds recorded inflows of ₹9,039 crore, compared with ₹7,973 crore in August, marking an all-time high. Mid-cap fund inflows rose to ₹7,835 crore from ₹6,989 crore in the previous month.
Large-cap funds saw inflows of ₹859.5 crore in September, reversing the net outflow of ₹1,147 crore recorded in August.
Suranjana Borthakur, Head of Distribution and Strategic Alliances at Mirae Asset Mutual Fund, said equity inflows were healthy across categories, with small-cap and mid-cap funds seeing higher inflows than in the previous month.
She also pointed to negative flows in hybrid funds, suggesting that some money may have moved out of these categories and been reallocated to equity schemes. However, the AMFI data alone does not establish the reason for the outflows.
Meanwhile, systematic Investment Plan (SIP) contributions stood at ₹32,490 crore, the highest on record, according to the data.
Equity exchange-traded funds (ETFs) attracted inflows of ₹9,960 crore in September, while gold and silver ETFs saw inflows of ₹4,451 crore and ₹1,974 crore, respectively. Gold ETF inflows rose from ₹2,597 crore in August.
Rohit Sarin, Co-Founder of Client Associates, said the September data reflected continued investor participation in equities, alongside flows into gold and silver ETFs. He said the trends highlighted the role of diversification, adding that investors should focus on asset allocation aligned with their financial goals, investment horizons and risk appetite rather than react to short-term market movements.
Agrim Verma, smallcase manager, Co-Founder - Divitiae Investments, said, "The strength of flows across equity categories suggests that retail investors are continuing to invest through the correction rather than retreating from equities."
Among other categories, credit risk funds recorded net inflows of ₹127.3 crore, compared with net outflows of ₹23 crore in August. New fund offer (NFO) inflows declined to ₹2,708 crore from ₹7,110 crore.
Corporate bond funds saw net outflows of ₹4,652 crore in September, higher than the ₹3,190 crore outflow in August.
The mutual fund industry's total assets under management (AUM) stood at ₹82.64 lakh crore at the end of September, compared with ₹87.07 lakh crore in August.

articles.title: Indian debt funds set to extend $4.5 billion bond selloff after RBI policy shift - The Hindu
articles.summary: Indian debt funds set to extend $4.5 billion bond selloff after RBI policy shift  The HinduIndia 10-year bond yield tops 7.35% as RBI's liquidity clamp down hurts  ET GovernmentLetters to Editor  BusinessLineRBI steps may help local bond market  The Economic TimesIndia 10Y Yield Hits 3-Year High  TradingView
articles.full_text:
Indian mutual funds are set to sell more government bonds after offloading $4.5 billion since July, four fund managers said, as the central bank's policy shift raised expectations of a longer, steeper rate-tightening cycle.
The Reserve Bank of India raised rates for the first time in nearly four years and signalled further increases as inflation rises.
Mutual funds have reduced their exposure to longer-dated government bonds as rate expectations have changed, said Mansi Sajeja, a fixed-income fund manager at SBI Mutual Fund.
Asset managers sold a net ₹51 billion ($527.08 million) of government bonds in the three sessions after the rate increase, adding to sales of ₹378 billion in July-September.
"The policy tone sounded more cautionary on inflation generalisation than growth outlook, giving it a hawkish tilt," Amit Somani, a deputy head of fixed income at Tata Asset Management said.
Mr. Somani expects long-term bond yields to rise to a range of 7.20%-7.40%.
The five-year bond yield topped 7.05%, rising by almost 70 basis points in two months, while the 10-year bond yield was close to 7.35% levels, highest in nearly three years.
"Several factors, including global rate hikes, multi-decade high global bond yields, expectations of an earlier-than-anticipated domestic rate-hike cycle, and continued uncertainty in energy markets, prompted mutual funds to reduce duration risk by trimming government bond exposure," said Vikas Garg, head of fixed income at Invesco Mutual Fund.
Heavy open market sale of bonds by the RBI and risks of a repeat of such operations have also altered demand-supply dynamics, fund managers said.
The RBI sold bonds worth ₹1 trillion last month, notching its highest net sale for any financial year in over a decade.
SHIFT TO SHORT-TERM ASSETS
While selling long duration government bonds, mutual funds are moving to ultra-short duration assets across government and corporate debt.
Axis Mutual Fund now prefers one-year to three-year high-quality corporate bonds, where favourable carry, ample liquidity and limited issuance of banks' certificates of deposit create an appealing opportunity, the fund house said in a note.
It may look to tactically add duration only when rate-hiking cycle progresses and yields become more attractive.
Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC likes the ultra-short term debt while Bandhan Asset Management has slashed its weighted average bond duration to less than a year, from around 12 years, the fund houses said in recent interviews with Reuters.

West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the benchmark US Crude Oil price – attracts fresh sellers during the Asian session on Tuesday, snapping a three-day winning streak to a two-week high, touched the previous day. The black liquid currently trades around the $91.75 region, down over 0.70% for the day, though the downside seems cushioned amid escalating Middle East conflicts.
The Iran-backed Houthi group in Yemen escalated its campaign against Saudi Arabia and fired more missiles on Monday. This follows deadly strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport over the weekend, which drew a Saudi vow of retaliation. Moreover, US President Donald Trump raised the possibility of joining strikes on the Houthi group and resuming attacks on Iran.
Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of violating an "energy ceasefire" announced by U.S. President Donald Trump. This keeps the geopolitical risk premium in play and should act as a tailwind for crude oil prices, warranting caution for bearish traders before confirming that the recent bounce from an over one-month low has run out of steam.
From a technical perspective, oil prices hold comfortably above the 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) at $82.75, retaining a constructive bullish bias despite the latest pullback. Moreover, the black liquid sits just over the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement at $91.27, suggesting an initial demand zone around the current area amid mixed momentum indicators on the daily chart.
The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) remains slightly below zero and hints at fading upside momentum, while the Relative Strength Index (RSI) near 52 reinforces a neutral-to-positive tone, indicating that bullish pressure persists but is no longer overstretched. Hence, weakness below the 38.2% Fibo. is needed to back the case for a further depreciating move.
This is followed by deeper Fibonacci floors at $87.85 and $84.43, with the 78.6% level at $79.57 and the prior cycle low at $73.37 marking more distant structural demand. On the topside, a break above the 23.6% Fibo. retracement at $95.49 would reopen the path toward the cycle high area near $102.33, which is likely to cap gains unless momentum meaningfully improves.
(The technical analysis of this story was written with the help of an AI tool. Know more.)
WTI daily chart
WTI Oil FAQs
WTI Oil is a type of Crude Oil sold on international markets. The WTI stands for West Texas Intermediate, one of three major types including Brent and Dubai Crude. WTI is also referred to as “light” and “sweet” because of its relatively low gravity and sulfur content respectively. It is considered a high quality Oil that is easily refined. It is sourced in the United States and distributed via the Cushing hub, which is considered “The Pipeline Crossroads of the World”. It is a benchmark for the Oil market and WTI price is frequently quoted in the media.
Like all assets, supply and demand are the key drivers of WTI Oil price. As such, global growth can be a driver of increased demand and vice versa for weak global growth. Political instability, wars, and sanctions can disrupt supply and impact prices. The decisions of OPEC, a group of major Oil-producing countries, is another key driver of price. The value of the US Dollar influences the price of WTI Crude Oil, since Oil is predominantly traded in US Dollars, thus a weaker US Dollar can make Oil more affordable and vice versa.
The weekly Oil inventory reports published by the American Petroleum Institute (API) and the Energy Information Agency (EIA) impact the price of WTI Oil. Changes in inventories reflect fluctuating supply and demand. If the data shows a drop in inventories it can indicate increased demand, pushing up Oil price. Higher inventories can reflect increased supply, pushing down prices. API’s report is published every Tuesday and EIA’s the day after. Their results are usually similar, falling within 1% of each other 75% of the time. The EIA data is considered more reliable, since it is a government agency.
OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) is a group of 12 Oil-producing nations who collectively decide production quotas for member countries at twice-yearly meetings. Their decisions often impact WTI Oil prices. When OPEC decides to lower quotas, it can tighten supply, pushing up Oil prices. When OPEC increases production, it has the opposite effect. OPEC+ refers to an expanded group that includes ten extra non-OPEC members, the most notable of which is Russia.

ISLAMABAD:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has revised upward Pakistan's inflation forecast to 9.9% but kept economic growth unchanged at 3.5%, suggesting that it has not agreed to the government's projections of relatively low inflation and high economic growth for this fiscal year.
The fresh figures have been released in the World Economic Outlook (WEO) report while the IMF's staff-level report will be made public only after the loan tranches are approved by the executive board tentatively late November. According to the WEO report, which the IMF released on Tuesday on the sidelines of annual meetings, inflation in Pakistan could accelerate to 9.9% in this fiscal year. In April this year, the IMF had projected Pakistan's inflation rate at 8.4% for fiscal year 2026-27, which it also maintained in July's report.
The IMF has not given any Pakistan-specific reasons for the increase in inflation rate but it has also revised upward the inflation projections for the Middle East and Central Asia region due to the ongoing conflict that has impacted energy supply and prices. The rate is higher than the official target of 8.2%. During the recently concluded staff-level talks, the federal government and the central bank had maintained that despite inflationary pressures Pakistan would be able to meet the annual target.
The 9.9% inflation projection means that the IMF might also be seeking higher interest rates to contain the inflationary pressures.
The government has been fully passing on the increase in fuel prices to domestic consumers in addition to charging heavy taxes. It has given Rs2,000 per month compensation to motorcyclists and Rs3,000 to small car owners. But the IMF has objected to the scheme, terming it broad and carrying high cost. The report underlined that global headline inflation rose in August, as energy prices bounced back following the short-lived ceasefire in the Middle East.
According to the IMF report, economic growth in Pakistan may remain at 3.5% in this fiscal year - a forecast that is unchanged compared to the lender's previous projections. During the review talks, Pakistani authorities had tried to convince the IMF that the annual growth target of 4% will be achieved.
In an interview with Reuters, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said that "I am still quite clear that we should clock north of 4%". Pakistan has been following a prolonged phase of economic stabilisation under three different IMF programmes, which according to the World Bank is one of the reasons for higher poverty in the country.
In his detailed memo, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal has recently recommended to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif an eight-point new Growth-Compatible Fiscal Stabilisation Framework for higher growth and development instead of merely saying in polls that we "inherited an economic crisis" and achieved stability.
He wrote to the prime minister last month that Pakistan was increasingly achieving fiscal stabilisation by compressing development expenditure and borrowing more, rather than sufficiently expanding the revenue base and increasing exports.
"The electorate will judge the government on the economy it experiences in 2029: growth, employment, income, investment, exports, inflation, energy costs and economic opportunity," he wrote.
The IMF has also projected a slightly higher current account deficit of 1% of the gross domestic product (GDP), or about $4.4 billion. It is around $450 million more than the IMF's previous projections. The IMF said that in the Middle East and Central Asia, growth is projected to drop to 0.3% in 2026 before rebounding to 6.3% in 2027. Relative to the April projection, this is a downward revision of 2.2 percentage points for 2026 and an upward revision of 1.7 percentage points for 2027, consistent with a longer closure of the Strait of Hormuz, compared with the baseline assumptions in the April report, and a corresponding larger rebound after the Strait reopens, it added.
But the lender said that the global economy was showing resilience, which is reflected in its latest global growth forecast. The new global growth projection remains broadly unchanged from April, despite a more persistent energy market disruption than anticipated. Global activity is projected to grow at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027.
Global headline inflation is projected to rise to 4.7% this year, reflecting primarily higher commodity prices, and to fall back to 4.1% in 2027; the pass-through to core inflation is expected to be limited.
The IMF said that global activity in the first half of 2026 held up better than expected despite the dragging war in the Middle East and continuing strains from trade tensions. The technology cycle has provided a demand impulse, driven by strong investment in artificial intelligence (AI). The interaction of these forces - geopolitics and technology - has produced a split global economy: favourable terms of trade or technology-related exports and investment give some countries a cushion, whereas others face higher import bills and weaker demand.
But it said that resilience was under strain. Without shoring up supply capacity and replenishing policy buffers, the global economy could soon test the limits of resilience. Inventories in energy markets are dwindling and additional geopolitical shocks could still transmit rapidly through prices and supply disruptions, it added.

articles.title: UK economy to suffer second-highest inflation in G7 - City AM
articles.summary: UK economy to suffer second-highest inflation in G7  City AM
articles.full_text:
The UK economy will suffer the second highest inflation of any G7 country over the next two years, the International Monetary Fund has warned, putting Chancellor John Healey’s efforts to ease the cost of living at risk.
In its latest report published today, the global finance body has said that inflation will remain above the Bank of England’s target two per cent rate for the seventh year running.
The fund’s officials said inflation would average at 3.3 per cent in 2026 and 2.8 per cent in 2027, remaining above almost all the world’s dominant economies.
Only the US will suffer from a higher rate of inflation this year while Germany will top the list of G7 countries next year.
Inflation in the UK was higher than all G7 members in 2025, underpinning policymakers’ battles with maintaining price stability. Interest rates are also forecast to remain higher for longer.
In more encouraging news for Healey, economists at the financial authority predicted the UK would have a higher growth rate than several of its European peers.
The IMF said that UK GDP growth would be the joint-second highest this year at a rate of 1.3 per cent before slowing to 1.2 per cent growth in 2027. Growth in the UK will be higher in both years than any country barring the US. Germany’s GDP is also expected to expand by 1.3 per cent this year.
While the growth forecast for 2026 was revised up by 0.3 percentage points compared to the last report in July, the estimate for 2027 was downgraded from 1.3 per cent.
On a per capita basis, the UK will still trail the likes of Italy, Canada and the US this year.
Inflation challenge to governments
Top officials from central banks and governments, including the Bank of England’s Andrew Bailey and Healey, are gathering in Thailand for a series of IMF meetings.
The world economic outlook report said that AI and related infrastructure was driving demand across the world while conflicts in Europe and the Middle East had hit supply of critical goods such as oil and gas.
While the global economy has managed to survive the impacts of recent economic shocks, there were “limits” to resilience given an AI investment boom could lead to higher prices and governments had less wriggle room to respond to shocks given high debt levels.
The IMF based its forecasts on the assumption that trading across the Strait of Hormuz would resume in March 2027 while changes in technology would moderate next year.
The report warned that growth would slow next year due to the impact of high energy prices and interest rates, with monetary policy in the UK set to be tighter than in other major economies.
The world economy is expected to grow by 3.1 per cent this year and 3.4 per cent in 2027.
Economists urged Healey and his peers to use any windfall revenues from growth and lower energy prices to reduce borrowing. The report said extra government spending to support households or businesses “should be used sparingly” and not “complicate the task of monetary policy”.
Bailey last week warned that the government had to remain vigilant and not leave the central bank to deal with risks to inflation and market stability.

articles.title: Trump Creates Committee to Investigate Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook: What’s at Stake - MundoNOW
articles.summary: Trump Creates Committee to Investigate Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook: What’s at Stake  MundoNOW
articles.full_text:
Posted on 10/12/26 at 21:07
President Donald Trump created a committee to investigate Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook and recommend whether there is «cause» to remove her from office. The memorandum, dated October 7 and released by the White House on Friday, October 9, schedules a closed-door hearing at the White House for November 5, two days after the midterm elections.
- The committee will investigate allegations that Cook made false statements in connection with «one or more mortgage instruments.» Cook denies wrongdoing.
- It consists of three Trump administration officials: Kevin Hassett, assistant to the president for economic policy; Andrea Lucas, chair of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC); and Keith Sonderling, director of the Office of Government Ethics, according to CNBC.
- No president has successfully removed a Federal Reserve governor.
Why it matters: the Federal Reserve sets interest rates that influence what consumers pay for mortgages, credit cards, and car loans. If a president can remove governors who participate in those decisions, investors may fear that monetary policy could become more vulnerable to political pressure.
What the Memo Says About Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook
The White House memorandum says the committee will advise the president on whether there is cause to remove Cook under the law governing the Federal Reserve, 12 U.S.C. §242, as interpreted by the Supreme Court in Trump v. Cook in 2026. The committee may consult with the Department of Justice.
Key dates:
- Up to 3 days before the hearing: Cook may submit a written statement responding to the allegations.
- November 5: a closed-door hearing will take place at the White House, will be transcribed, and may last no more than four hours. Cook must appear and may be represented by an attorney.
- November 10: deadline for Cook to submit a final written statement.
- Afterward: the committee will send Trump its factual findings, legal conclusions, and a recommendation on whether cause exists for her removal. The memorandum does not set a deadline for Trump’s final decision.
How We Got Here
Trump attempted to remove Cook in August 2025 after Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte accused her of making false statements in mortgage documents. Cook sued, and a federal court blocked her removal. In June of this year, the Supreme Court declined to lift that injunction, ruling that Cook was entitled to notice and an opportunity to respond before she could be removed. The court did not prevent Trump from beginning a new process that complies with those requirements. If Trump ultimately removes her again, the dispute is likely to return to court, CNBC noted.
Cook, who was appointed by former President Joe Biden, has a permanent vote on Federal Reserve interest-rate decisions as a member of the Board of Governors. Trump has criticized what he calls a «hostile» Fed, now chaired by Kevin Warsh, for not lowering interest rates.
What It Means for Your Wallet
At its September 16 meeting, the Fed raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point, to a range of 3.75% to 4%, in a 12-0 vote, according to its official statement. The next meeting is scheduled for October 27 and 28.
The average rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage reached 7.40% on October 8, according to Freddie Mac’s weekly survey. The committee investigating Cook does not directly change those rates, but uncertainty over the Fed’s independence could affect the returns investors demand on longer-term debt.
What You Can Do
- If you’re buying a home or refinancing, compare offers from at least three lenders and ask how much it costs to lock in an interest rate for 30 to 60 days.
- If you carry variable-rate credit card debt, prioritize paying it down: those rates are influenced by changes in the Fed’s benchmark rate.
- Mark October 28: that is when the Fed is scheduled to announce its next monetary policy decision.
Sources: White House, memo of October 7, 2026; Federal Reserve, statement of September 16; Federal Reserve, calendar; Freddie Mac PMMS; CNBC; NBC News. Data consulted on October 10, 2026.

articles.title: Southeast Asia boosts KF-21 push as Korea leverages T-50, FA-50 foothold - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
articles.summary: Southeast Asia boosts KF-21 push as Korea leverages T-50, FA-50 foothold - CHOSUNBIZ  Chosunbiz
articles.full_text:
As several Southeast Asian countries increase defense spending and move to replace aging fighter jets, Korea's KF-21 is emerging as a new export market. The defense industry plans to target the main fighter market as well, following the FA-50 light attack aircraft and the T-50 advanced trainer already being exported to Southeast Asia.
According to the defense industry on the 13th, the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) said in its report on global military expenditure trends released in April that Southeast Asian countries' military expenditure last year was $67.1 billion (about 89.88 trillion won), up 15% from the previous year. Compared with 2016, it increased 43% in nine years. As military buildup to counter security instability coincides with the replacement of aging equipment, fighter jet purchases are also continuing.
◇ Sold 78 T-50s and FA-50s in Southeast Asia… a "stepping-stone" for KF-21 exports
Southeast Asian countries that are recently increasing defense spending are pushing to introduce fighter jets in the dozens. The Philippines decided to introduce 40 multirole fighters, and Malaysia is reviewing a plan to secure 36 next-generation fighters. Indonesia is said to have drawn up a plan to introduce 48 KF-21s. Based on this, Korea's securities industry analyzed total Southeast Asian demand for fighter introductions at more than 120 aircraft.
Analysts say Korean defense companies have secured an advantageous position in the Southeast Asian market. They have already supplied trainers and light attack aircraft, securing an operational foothold. Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI)(047810) Industries (KAI) signed contracts to supply a total of 78 aircraft: 22 T-50i to Indonesia, 14 T-50TH to Thailand, 24 FA-50 to the Philippines, and 18 FA-50 to Malaysia.
Moreover, the T-50 and FA-50 are regarded as a "stepping-stone" helping the KF-21 enter the market. Because of their limited force size, Southeast Asian countries often use a single type for multiple missions, including training and light attack. For that reason, when choosing a new fighter, how naturally it connects with existing pilot training systems, weapons operations, and maintenance infrastructure becomes a key criterion, the industry said.
A KAI official said, "Southeast Asian countries often use one type as both a trainer and a fighter," and noted, "With that in mind, we are emphasizing interoperability with existing T-50 and FA-50 family aircraft in the process of exporting the KF-21." Malaysia is scheduled to receive its first two FA-50M aircraft at the end of this month. Whether it will procure more is expected to depend on various forms of support after delivery.
◇ Rafale has proven performance in combat… military operation, a KF-21 "export record"
France's Rafale, cited as a competitor to the KF-21 in the Southeast Asian market, has leveraged real combat experience as an export strength. The French military deployed the Rafale for close air support, precision strikes, and reconnaissance in Afghanistan, Libya, and Mali. Manufacturer Dassault Aviation has highlighted this operational record as evidence that its precision-strike, long-range attack, and intelligence collection capabilities have been verified on the battlefield.
For the KF-21, which has not yet seen combat, the South Korean Air Force's operational record is expected to play that role. The first mass-production unit, No. 001, was delivered to the Air Force for the first time at KAI's Sacheon plant on the 22nd of last month and moved to its first operating base, Yecheon. With development completed, the KF-21 has moved into actual Air Force operation. KAI plans to hand over eight aircraft to the Air Force by the end of the year, and the Air Force plans to deploy them in actual missions from the second half of next year.
The industry believes the Air Force's operational records, which will accumulate from now on, can be used directly for overseas exports. Actual operations will reveal whether the aircraft can reliably carry out repeated sorties and maintain a certain availability rate. Interoperability and operational efficiency when conducting missions alongside existing fighters are also expected to be confirmed.
According to the industry, potential buyers in Southeast Asia are watching this process. A defense industry official said, "Interest is quite high," and added, "Beyond the fact that development succeeded, showing that the South Korean Air Force operates it without issues will become another 'export record.'"
Indonesia, the KF-21's co-developing country, is considered the most advanced candidate as the first overseas customer. It initially planned to introduce 48 aircraft, but is currently pushing a first contract for 16. Indonesia's state-owned aerospace company PTDI signed an agreement with KAI last month to produce 15% of the airframe structures. The project is worth about $2.9 billion. KAI aims to sign the main contract within the year.

articles.title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6981 – Reuters estimate - investingLive
articles.summary: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6981 – Reuters estimate  investingLive
articles.full_text:
Summary
- PBOC CNY reference rate setting for the trading session ahead.
The fixing mechanism matters most right now because its message has shifted over the past month. For nearly a year, the PBOC has set its daily guidance weaker than market expectations, which traders read as an effort to slow the yuan's appreciation, and in late August that gap reached its widest since February, shortly after the yuan touched a three-and-a-half-year high. Through September, however, the midpoint has strengthened at a faster pace, narrowing its gap with market expectations and suggesting the central bank has eased its resistance to yuan gains. The fixing is still set weaker than models imply, so this looks like a loosening of the brakes rather than their removal. The balance Beijing is weighing is unchanged: a firmer currency supports capital stability and import costs, but too rapid a rise risks eroding export competitiveness while the domestic economy remains soft. The gap between each day's fixing and consensus estimates remains one of the clearest guides to how far the PBOC is willing to let the yuan run.
---
Earlier:
---
The daily fixing is Beijing's quietest but clearest tool for telling markets how fast it wants the yuan to move, and after months of saying slow down, it has lately been saying go, gradually.
Summary:
- The PBOC sets the daily USD/CNY reference rate, or midpoint, at around 0115 GMT, one of the most closely watched signals in Asian FX markets.
- China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, allowing the yuan to trade within a band of plus or minus 2% around the daily midpoint during onshore hours.
- The midpoint reflects a mix of inputs, including the prior day's close, moves in major currencies, broader international FX conditions and domestic factors such as capital flows and growth momentum, with policymakers retaining discretion over the final number.
- If market pressure pushes the yuan toward either edge of the band, the PBOC can intervene through direct buying or selling of yuan, liquidity adjustments, or guidance via state-owned banks.
- A stronger-than-expected fixing typically signals the PBOC is leaning against depreciation, while a weaker fixing can indicate tolerance for a softer currency or discomfort with the pace of gains.
- For nearly a year the fixing has been set weaker than market estimates, with the gap reaching its widest since February in late August.
- In September the PBOC strengthened the fixing for eight straight sessions, the longest run since 2023, and the midpoint reached its strongest level since February 2023.
- The yuan has pushed to its strongest levels since early 2023 onshore and since mid-2022 offshore, with Goldman Sachs expecting Beijing to remain comfortable with sustained but gradual appreciation.
The People's Bank of China sets the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT, a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. It has taken on added significance in recent weeks as policymakers have shifted from restraining the yuan's rise to guiding it higher.
China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the yuan is allowed to trade within a band of plus or minus 2% around the central midpoint set each trading day. That midpoint reflects a mix of inputs, including the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies such as the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic considerations like capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The calculation is not purely mechanical, giving policymakers room to use the fixing to guide market expectations.
Once the midpoint is set, onshore USD/CNY trades freely within the allowable range. Should market pressure push the currency toward either edge of that band, the central bank can step in to smooth volatility, whether through direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance channelled through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often read as a policy signal rather than a purely technical reference point. A stronger-than-expected midpoint typically suggests the PBOC is leaning against depreciation, while a weaker fixing can signal tolerance for a softer currency, or unease with how quickly the yuan is rising.
That second reading has dominated for much of the past year. For nearly a year, the central bank set its daily guidance weaker than market expectations, a pattern traders and analysts interpreted as an attempt to slow the yuan's appreciation. The gap reached its widest since February in late August, shortly after the yuan touched a three-and-a-half-year high against the dollar.
September has brought a clear change of tone. The midpoint has strengthened at a faster pace this month, narrowing its gap with market expectations and suggesting the PBOC has eased its resistance to yuan gains. The central bank strengthened the fixing for eight consecutive sessions, the longest streak since 2023, and the midpoint has since reached its strongest level since February 2023. The onshore yuan has traded at its strongest since January 2023, while the offshore rate has reached levels last seen in July 2022. Even so, the fixing is still being set well weaker than market estimates, with one recent midpoint more than 500 pips below a Reuters survey forecast, a reminder that Beijing is allowing appreciation on its own terms rather than stepping aside.
The underlying tension is a familiar one. A firmer yuan supports capital stability and eases import costs, but a rapid rise risks undermining export competitiveness at a moment when China's broader economy continues to show signs of softness. For traders and investors, the gap between each day's fixing and consensus estimates remains one of the clearest windows into how Beijing is weighing that trade-off, and whether the recent green light for gains stays in place once the summit has passed.

articles.title: Gold Prices Slip From Overnight Peak as Dollar and Oil Gains Pressure Bullion - azat.tv
articles.summary: Gold Prices Slip From Overnight Peak as Dollar and Oil Gains Pressure Bullion  azat.tv
articles.full_text:
Spot and Futures Reversal After Overnight High
Spot gold fell $28.91, or 0.69%, to close at $4,164.96 an ounce on Monday, October 12, 2026, according to That’s TradingNEWS. The precious metal opened the week attempting a recovery, pushing toward an overnight high of $4,218.10 in early Asian trade before giving back $53 from that peak. December Comex gold futures dropped 0.57% to settle at $4,192.30 near midday in New York. The pullback erased the gains from late last week, when gold had climbed more than 1% to a one-week high following a softer dollar and declining oil prices.
Monday’s reversal left traders viewing Friday’s rally as a temporary short-covering bounce inside an ongoing downtrend rather than a structural market shift. The broader context remains severe for the non-yielding asset, which now trades 25.5% below its record peak of $5,589.38 reached on January 28, 2026. Over the past month, gold is down 3.12%, reflecting sustained selling pressure as macroeconomic conditions favor higher-yielding instruments.
Macroeconomic Headwinds: Dollar Strength and Rising Oil
The primary catalysts behind Monday’s decline were a strengthening U.S. dollar and a reversal in crude oil markets. The U.S. dollar index climbed above 102.4 during the session, marking its strongest level since April 2025. A firmer dollar increases the cost of bullion for buyers holding other major currencies, dampening physical and investment demand globally. Meanwhile, crude oil futures reversed earlier losses following renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, with West Texas Intermediate trading up 2.01% at $93.70 a barrel by midday.
The oil market reversal undermined earlier optimism driven by proposed diesel supply agreements and regional energy talks. Initial market relief faded as analysts calculated that the announced volumes covered only a fraction of daily global consumption. As oil prices ticked higher, inflation concerns resurfaced, removing the downward pressure on energy costs that had briefly supported gold late last week.
Federal Reserve Expectations and the 10-Year Treasury Yield Squeeze
The opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion remains a central hurdle for investors. Traders are currently pricing an 85% probability of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike by December, keeping the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield elevated at 5.24%. With the benchmark yield sitting near 24-year highs reached earlier in October, institutional allocators face substantial forgone income on risk-free debt.
Holding one ounce of gold at $4,164.96 translates into giving up more than $218 annually in risk-free income at a 5.24% yield. This rising real-rate squeeze, combined with synchronized selling across global bond markets, leaves few alternative safe havens for institutional capital, continuing to pressure precious metals through the final quarter of 2026.
Geopolitical Tensions and the War Premium Paradox
Geopolitical instability failed to provide traditional safe-haven support for bullion as Middle East escalations drove energy markets higher instead. Over the weekend, reported Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia’s main airport resulted in 12 fatalities, prompting discussions of potential U.S. military participation in retaliatory actions. Concurrently, regional diplomatic friction persisted, including the rejection of peace terms by Iran and continuing strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure despite earlier ceasefire announcements.
Historically, conflict headlines would drive immediate capital flows into precious metals. However, the transmission channel in 2026 runs primarily through crude oil and headline inflation expectations. Because higher oil prices reinforce monetary tightening by central banks, geopolitical escalation directly undermines gold by pushing real yields and the U.S. dollar higher.
Silver Underperformance and the Gold-Silver Ratio
Precious metals weakness extended across the broader sector, with silver underperforming gold on nearly every major timeframe. Spot silver traded down $0.54, or 0.89%, to $60.26 an ounce on Monday, bringing its year-to-date decline to 14.62%. The gold-silver ratio hovered near 69.1, reflecting sustained industrial demand concerns and heightened risk aversion among market participants.
Silver’s tendency to amplify gold’s losses was evident during recent selloffs, where industrial exposure added downward momentum. Platinum group metals faced similar pressures, with platinum and palladium posting weekly losses as high interest rates and elevated energy costs dampened manufacturing and automotive demand.
Outlook and Upcoming Inflation Catalysts
Market attention now shifts toward upcoming macroeconomic data releases from the Bureau of Labor Statistics and the Census Bureau, led by the consumer price index report. Economists forecast a headline inflation rate of 3.7% year-over-year, which could cement expectations for further monetary tightening. A hotter-than-expected print would likely drive December rate-hike odds even higher, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield above its recent band and challenging critical downside support levels for gold near $4,050 to $4,100.
Conversely, a softer inflation reading could trigger a substantial relief rally by reducing policy pressures and weakening the dollar index. Until a decisive shift in central bank policy or real yields materializes, gold remains tightly bound to the competing forces of dollar strength, energy-driven inflation, and elevated risk-free borrowing costs.

articles.full_text:
Oswal Pumps Limited submitted its Q4 FY2026 Monitoring Agency report to BSE and NSE on May 08, 2026, as required under SEBI Regulation 32. ICRA Limited, the appointed Monitoring Agency, confirmed no material deviation in IPO proceeds utilisation, though it flagged that purchases under certain capital expenditure objects do not align with vendor specifications in the prospectus. Out of total gross proceeds of INR 890.00 crore monitored, cumulative utilisation reached INR 618.650 crore by March 31, 2026, with INR 271.350 crore remaining unutilised and deployed in fixed deposits and bank balances with a market value of INR 279.827 crore.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.
Oswal Pumps Limited filed its Monitoring Agency (MA) report for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 with BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited on May 08, 2026. The submission was made pursuant to Regulation 32 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. ICRA Limited, appointed as the Monitoring Agency under an agreement dated May 26, 2025, prepared the report to track the utilisation of proceeds raised through the company's Initial Public Offer of Equity Shares.
IPO Issue Details
The IPO, which opened on June 13, 2025 and closed on June 17, 2025, comprised an issue of 22,595,114 equity shares of face value of INR 1 each, aggregating up to INR 1387.34 crore. The following key financial parameters characterise the issue:

Monitoring Agency Findings
ICRA's report confirms no material deviation in the utilisation of IPO proceeds relative to the objects of the issue. All government and statutory approvals related to the objects have been obtained, the means of finance for the disclosed objects remain unchanged, and no major deviation was observed over earlier monitoring agency reports. However, ICRA noted that purchases made under the capital expenditure objects — specifically "Funding certain capital expenditure of Company" and "Investment in Oswal Solar for setting up new manufacturing units" — do not align with the vendor specifications proposed in the prospectus.
